name: SiegeWeaponSpot - Default (seed v1)
description: A place reserved for a siege weapon in a scenario, owned by one team. Created from the scenario's Siege weapons step.

steps.description: Name the spot and pick the team it belongs to.

fields.label: Scenario
fields.description: Filled in from the scenario you are editing.

fields.label: Team
fields.description: Only this team can place a weapon here. Attackers and defenders can both have spots.

fields.label: Name
fields.description: Shown in the spot picker, e.g. 'North wall tower'.

fields.label: Order
fields.description: Leave empty to add it after the existing spots.

steps.description: Where the weapon goes. Draw a box-shaped WorldGuard region for the spot with the region task (or pick an existing region) and choose the way the weapon faces. The size class is worked out from the region and the facing, and the region's floor and space are checked; both need the Minecraft server (the floor and space check also siege.weapons.enabled). A region you draw is renamed to siege_spot_<id> when you save.

fields.label: Region
fields.description: The spot's WorldGuard region. Draw a box (a cuboid selection) exactly as big as the weapon may be, with its bottom on the layer the weapon stands on: Small 7 x 9 x 5, Medium 7 x 9 x 8, Large 9 x 15 x 16 (width across x length along the facing x height). A polygon counts as its bounding box. A region you draw is renamed to siege_spot_<id> when you save; running this step again on a saved spot replaces that region. A region you select is used as it is.

fields.label: Facing
fields.description: The direction the weapon points (the way it shoots); it is rotated to face this way. The size class is measured across and along this direction, so changing it can change the class.

fields.label: Size class
fields.description: Worked out on save from the region's bounds and the facing: the largest class that fits (Small 7 x 9 x 5, Medium 7 x 9 x 8, Large 9 x 15 x 16, width across x length along the facing x height). A region smaller than Small is refused. When the Minecraft server can't be asked, the class stays as it was and is checked again when a weapon is placed.
